title: Exchange Variation
intro: 3.exd5: take back with the c-pawn, develop the knights and pin with ...Bg4.

lessons.title: Take with the c-pawn
lessons.summary: Keep a pawn in the centre, then hit d4.

steps.text: 3.exd5 is the Exchange Variation. White releases the tension.
Take back so you keep a pawn in the centre.
steps.ifWrong: 3...cxd5 keeps a pawn in the centre and opens the c-file.
steps.ifRight: The c-file is open for your rook, and the position is calm and equal.

feedback.d8d5: 3...Qxd5 brings the queen out early. Taking with the c-pawn keeps a pawn in the centre.

steps.text: Develop and put pressure on d4.
steps.ifRight: Next ...Bg4 pins the knight that defends d4.

steps.text: Your knight hits d4, and the open c-file waits for a rook.
White plays 4.Bd3 instead. Develop with the same idea.
steps.hint: Bring a knight out towards d4.

lessons.title: Pin the defender: ...Bg4
lessons.summary: The knight on f3 guards d4. Pin it.

steps.text: 5.Bb5 pins your knight to the king.
Pin back. The knight on f3 is the main guard of d4.
steps.ifRight: d4 has one defender less, and you develop easily.

steps.text: The bishop sits outside the pawn chain, where it belongs in the Caro-Kann.
5.Nc3 develops instead and adds pressure on d5.

steps.ifWrong: 5...Bg4 pins the knight and adds pressure on d4.
steps.ifRight: Same idea, whatever White's fifth move.

steps.text: This came from 2.Nf3 d5 3.exd5 cxd5 4.d4 Nc6 5.Nc3. Find the pin.
steps.hint: The knight on f3 guards d4.
steps.ifRight: Different order, same position, same plan.

lessons.title: 4.Nc3: guard d5 first
lessons.summary: Develop the king's knight to guard d5, then pin.

steps.text: Pin the knight and keep an eye on d4.
steps.ifRight: The bishop is outside the pawn chain, where it belongs.

steps.text: Next come ...e6 and ...Nc6. Your pieces develop easily.
Another route: 2.Nc3 d5 3.exd5 cxd5 4.d4. Find the developing move that guards d5.
steps.ifRight: This is the same position as 3.exd5 cxd5 4.Nc3 Nf6.
